subject: Fitting models with integrals over a lognormal field

messages.author: 5f6425ab97f885a0
messages.subject: Fitting models with integrals over a lognormal field
parts:
Hi,

Does R-INLA allow one to fit models where observations (yi's) are related to linear combinations of the exponent of the latent Gaussian field (x)? Specifically, I'm working on an application where the yi's are noisy observations of integrals over exp(x) where x is the latent Gaussian field that I'm trying to infer/reconstruct.

In my understanding, the 2009 Approximate Bayesian Inference for Latent Gaussian Models using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations paper doesn't seem to preclude this category of models. While I am new to R-INLA, I noticed most of the examples I could find involved cases where each yi is some function of xi (the value of the LGF at position i) with added effects.

I was wondering if another option to encode the dependence of yi's on multiple xi's could be encoded by somehow modifying the A matrix returned by inla.spde.make.A. The problem here appeared to be that the A matrix seems to encode dependence on the Gaussian field directly and not on the exponent of the Gaussian field, which is what I'd require.

I'd be grateful to know whether INLA as a method can be used for such a model , and, if so, does R-INLA currently allow one to do this?

Thank You.
Best,
Nayantara

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting models with integrals over a lognormal field
parts:
Hi,

the R-INLA implementation itself doesn't support predictors of the type a1*exp(x1)+a2*exp(x2) that you describe, but
the inlabru package allows iterative linearisation of such models, by iterated calls to inla().
You'd need a more recent version than currently on cran; the latest github release is 2.2.4, but I'm releasing 2.2.5 later today (you can install the devel version 2.2.4.9000)
See examples under Articles on https://inlabru-org.github.io/inlabru/

In essence, you'd need to specify model components, for a spatial model typically
  components =  ~ -1 + Intercept(1) + field(coordinates, model=spde_model)
and then the predictor can be a general R expression, like
  formula = response ~ A_function(.data.) %*% exp(Intercept + field.latent)
where A_function calculates the matrix that should be applied.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting models with integrals over a lognormal field
parts:
Hi,

I'm working on a 3D mesh addon that currently lives in a separate add-on package:
  https://github.com/finnlindgren/inlamesh3d
It doesn't have a fancy mesh generator, so you might need to supply your own tetrahedral mesh (R has n-dimensional delaunay available, so if you have lattice points that can be used).
Given a tetrahedral mesh, it constructs the finite element matrices needed for the Matern SPDE models.

Often a useful alternative that is much simpler and already available is to use a 2D mesh and then a kronecker precision model with the "group" feature. The resulting covariance isn't isotropic, but often 3D models shouldn't really be isotropic anyway...

You can also build your own model with inla.generic().  Such models can also be handled in inlabru by defining a "bru_mapper" that knows how to compute the A-matrix mapping etc.
This is quite new and I don't have any full examples yet.

Finn
